scope: Why Grow Your Own only; user-requested positive savings message, introduction hook and supplied seasonal paragraph

lead.before: There is something rather satisfying about putting supper on the table and knowing that you grew part of it. You chose the crop, looked after it and picked it when it was ready. That small piece of independence is a good enough reason to begin.
lead.after: There is something rather satisfying about putting supper on the table and knowing that you grew part of it. You chose the crop, looked after it and picked it when it was ready. That small piece of independence is a good enough reason to begin. And here are a few others:

before.title: Keep the sums sensible
before.text: Growing food can save money, but a shed full of expensive equipment will take some paying back. Start with a few useful tools, reuse sound materials and make compost. Put your best ground into crops that your household enjoys and will actually use. A modest bed of regularly picked salads can earn its place very quickly.

after.title: Save money from the start
after.text: You can begin growing with a very basic set of tools, and you can save money by making your own compost and reusing materials you already have. Grow the vegetables your household enjoys most. A small bed of salads, picked regularly, can provide plenty of fresh leaves and save you buying them each week.

before.title: Enjoy what the season gives you
before.text: Home growing brings abundance and gaps, sometimes in the same week. Pick little and often, share what you cannot use, and plan for the crops that follow. The individual guides include harvesting and storage advice; use it before the whole bed is ready at once.

after.title: Enjoy what the season gives you
after.text: Home growing brings abundance and gaps, sometimes in the same week. Eating with the seasons brings challenges but it also has its rewards. You will discover, for instance, why our ancestors feasted in the autumn and midwinter - because food is in surplus after the harvest. And why our bodies naturally become more active in the springtime. (Clue: Digging is physical work!)
